Definition: from G2007; an imposition (of hands officially):--laying (putting) on.
BiblicalUsage: Epithesis is the laying on of hands — the imposition by which gifts are given and ministries confirmed. Simon sees that through laying on of the apostles' hands the Holy Ghost is given; Timothy is told to neglect not the gift given him by prophecy, with the laying on of the hands of the presbytery; and Paul tells him to stir up the gift of God which is in thee by the putting on of my hands.
TheologicalSignificance: Hands, prayer, and a gift that must be stirred up, not left to cool — that is what the laying on of hands means. I believe the gift is real and the church stands behind it, and Timothy's charge is mine: stir up what God has given.
